rationale: This harness installs plugins, skills, agents and rules into the user's global OpenCode config, and its local plugins run with filesystem and shell access inside every project the user opens. A transitive dependency here reaches further than one in an ordinary application: a compromised package runs in every session, in every repo, with the user's own permissions. The default is therefore zero, and every exception is a recorded decision rather than an inference from a lockfile.

ruleNotes.maxDirectDependencies: Zero, not 'few'. At zero, every audit question, advisory and lockfile-integrity concern disappears entirely; at one, none of them do. That discontinuity is why the bar is a count and not a judgement call. The installer core already proves zero is achievable here — it uses native JSON.parse and fetch() rather than pulling in a JSON parser or an HTTP client.
ruleNotes.allowNativeModules: A native module runs node-gyp at install time, which is arbitrary code execution during `npm install`, before anybody has reviewed anything. Requires an explicit allowlist entry naming who approved it.
ruleNotes.requireExactVersions: A caret range means a fresh install can silently adopt a version nobody reviewed. Exact pins plus Dependabot gives reproducibility AND upgrades; pins alone rot, ranges alone are unreviewed.
ruleNotes.requireLockfileIntegrity: An entry without `resolved` + `integrity` is one npm cannot verify the contents of when it downloads it.
ruleNotes.maxAuditSeverity: The advisory level at which CI fails, if a lockfile ever exists to audit.

allowlistContract.purpose: An allowlist entry is a recorded human decision, not a mute button. It must name who approved it, when, and why — so a reviewer can go and ask that person, and so an entry that has outlived its reason is visible rather than invisible.

exampleEntry._comment: Documentation only — this key is not read by the checker. Copy this shape into `allowlist` above to request an exemption.
exampleEntry.scope: why it is needed, in one phrase
exampleEntry.reason: What this buys that native Node cannot, and why the wider reach is acceptable.

rules: An entry with enabled:false is ignored — the dependency will fail the check.
An entry missing any required field is rejected and reported, never treated as approval. A half-filled exemption is how a policy quietly becomes decorative.
approvedBy must be a person. 'team', 'automation', 'ci' or a bot name is not an approver.
reviewBy is optional; when set and in the past, the check warns so stale approvals surface instead of ossifying.
Adding an entry is a reviewed commit. Editing this file IS the approval step — do not weaken the rules to make a build pass.
